reasoning: Set A is a careful design (brief, spec, architecture with 20 ADs, package contracts, pipelines and tests), but it stops before the build starts. Its roadmap has four stages marked 'Specced' and no milestones. There is no tasks/plan.md, no todo.md, no CONSTRAINTS.md, no AGENTS.md and no context packets, and plan_snapshot.json has no milestones or tasks. So milestone quality, the dependency graph, task buildability and finding the next build step all fail outright. Its three probes have not been run ('Verdict: —'), and they check delistings against the assistant's own list (Lehman, Enron, WorldCom, Twitter…) instead of the user's ten names. Its roadmap also leaves the null-hypothesis-testing skill out of S2, even though PL-17's `decide` step uses it. Set B takes the plan to a buildable M1. It has a walking-skeleton milestone with a Phase-0 interface task, XS spine and thicken tasks, wiring tasks, a system task last, a full dependency graph with mitigations, and complete packets. Its packets carry the frozen types, signatures, golden cases and acceptance checks. The user's ten delisted names run through the spec, the tests and the samples. B's PCA is fitted per 252-day window, its spine baselines are real, and both skills are named in S2 to S4. B has weaknesses too. It splits stage 4 into two stages (S4 and S5), and its brief drops paper trading. Its probes were run against a local mock and report fail, yet carry 'Status: Ready'. references.md labels the milestones S2/S3 while the roadmap puts them on M4/M5. Its plan Scope has a very long Deferred list. B still wins clearly.
